faults.quote: Is that structure MECE — what overlaps, and what's missing? And which branch would you prioritize first, and why?
faults.why: This one turn stacks several questions (MECE, overlaps, gaps, priority, why), and the candidate stalled on it.

faults.quote: An exhibit for you — Hub–Lakeport — Economics of one one-way flight, FY2023 vs. FY2025 ($).
faults.why: The candidate asked only whether a competitor had entered and what it charges. The Lakeport per-flight exhibit was handed over unasked.

faults.quote: what would you want to understand about why Larkspur's fares fell?
faults.why: The same turn had just released the reason the fares fell (Larkspur matched the low-cost entrant), so the question reads wrong.

faults.quote: Now, an exhibit: Proposed new routes — Planning estimates (average per flight across Hub–Ashford and Hub–Brookhaven).
faults.why: The candidate never asked about new routes or redeployment. Handing over the new-routes exhibit gives away the solution path before the candidate got there.

faults.quote: Hub–Port Avery shows the same pattern: 80 seats, a 75% load factor and $20 of extras per passenger
faults.why: The candidate asked about load factors and passenger mix (business-heavy before?). Only load factor was answered. Passenger mix got no 'I don't have that'.

faults.quote: Earlier you said "× $200 - $9,200 = $400 per flight, so $1.4M, and we'd be roughly breakeven"
faults.why: The quoted figure is truncated: it starts mid-expression without the '48', so it reads oddly.

faults.quote: Then tell me the single biggest risk to your recommendation.
faults.why: The candidate had just named risks in t21 (unproven $180 fare, entrant attacking a third route). This re-asks the risk.

faults.quote: If you had to guard against that, how would you do it?
faults.why: The candidate's last answer already gave a mitigation ('I'd pilot one route first').
